intro.data: A functor copies a whole world into another. Here the List functor wraps each type in a list, and each function into "apply it to every element." Map each source piece to its image.
intro.alchemy: A functor copies a whole world into another. Here the Bundle functor wraps each material into a bundle, and each apparatus into "apply it to each." Map each source piece to its image.
intro.spellcraft: A functor copies a whole world into another. Here the Set functor wraps each essence into a set, and each rune into "cast it on each." Map each source piece to its image.
intro.abstract: A functor F sends each object and morphism of C to one in D. Map each source piece to its image under F.

goal.data: Map A and B to their list versions, and f to its mapped version.
goal.alchemy: Map A and B to their bundled versions, and f to its per-element version.
goal.spellcraft: Map A and B to their set versions, and f to its per-element version.
goal.abstract: Map A → F(A), B → F(B), and f → F(f).

afterSuccess.data: You mapped a whole little world into another: each type to its list, and the function to "map" of it. That assignment is a functor.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You mapped a whole little world into another: each material to its bundle, and the apparatus to its per-element form. That assignment is a functor.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You mapped a whole little world into another: each essence to its set, and the rune to its per-element form. That assignment is a functor.
afterSuccess.abstract: You mapped a whole little world into another, sending objects to objects and morphisms to morphisms. That assignment is a functor.

reveal.summary: A functor F : C → D sends each object A to F(A) and each morphism f : A → B to F(f) : F(A) → F(B) — it preserves sources and targets.
reveal.moreFormal: A functor must also preserve identities and composition: F(id_A) = id_F(A) and F(g ∘ f) = F(g) ∘ F(f). The app checks the structural part — that every image points the right way.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: List is a functor: List<A>, and map(f): List<A> => List<B>.
